chapter: Hampton and Basie: tours and road life
title: Royal's role in hiring; Basie drummers
summary: Royal only recommended; Willard Alexander or the manager hired; the Basie drummers Gus Johnson, Sonny Payne, Rufus and Harold Jones.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Right, right. During the time you were there, when there were new people coming into the band, did you usually do the hiring?

I wouldn't -- at times, if it was a wide-open space type of recommendation, yes, I would recommend. But I would have no business with any firing or hiring outright with nobody's band, never. I will never be the one to have somebody hired, fired. I may recommend, but I wouldn't do any hiring. Never firing. I wouldn't fire a dog.
Oh, he would have to do the hiring, or else get the manager to hire him. Sometimes Willard Alexander (PHONETIC), anybody, or his road manager, anybody. But he always kept the weight off of himself.
During the time that you were there, Sonny Payne (PHONETIC) was the drummer most of the time, wasn't he?
When I first went there, Gus Johnson was the drummer. Following that, it was Sonny Payne most of the

After that, Harold Jones (PHONETIC) came into the band. No, after that, Rufus Jones (PHONETIC) came into the band, out of the Ellington orchestra. Then he went back into the Ellington orchestra after that, Rufus Jones. Harold Jones came into the band.
And it was during that period, too, that -- when you were (inaudible)?
He'd made a trip. Louie Bellson made a trip with us over there, but that was a thing like four, five, six weeks or something. He was never a regular in the Basie band. He worked there for a trip.
During the time when Sonny Payne was incapacitated for some little thing.
